title: Priority Matrix Bubble Explorer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Data Visualization; Instructional Design
description: Interactive Chart.js bubble chart of eight invented MicroSim types plotted by effort and impact, with bubble size for count and color for status. Learners select and move items across the quadrant midpoints and see the quadrant list and a why-explanation update.

educational.audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners
learningObjectives: The learner will compare candidate items by impact, effort and frequency, and identify which quadrant each item occupies and why.
prerequisites: Bubble data as { x, y, r } objects

simulation.model: Two-by-two priority matrix with midpoint 5 on both axes
equations: radius = minR + (count - minCount) / (maxCount - minCount) * (maxR - minR), with minR = 4 x scale and maxR = 15 x scale

pedagogical.interactionPattern: Select, move, observe quadrant change, explain
keyQuestions: Which criterion separates two items that sit in different quadrants?
Should bubble size change a build-first decision?
commonMisconceptions: Bubble radius is proportional to the quantity it encodes (readers perceive area).
An item exactly on the midpoint belongs to the high side.
assessmentOpportunities: Name an item's quadrant from its scores and justify it
Compare two items on all three variables
